ns0:entry.ns0:title: perf(unitree_g1): cap ONNX Runtime thread pool for the G1 controllers…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
perf(unitree_g1): cap ONNX Runtime thread pool for the G1 controllers (#4264)

Add make_ort_session_options() to g1_utils and use it in every controller that
opens an ONNX session: GR00T (balance + walk), Holosoma, and the SONIC decoder.
These are small MLPs stepped at 50 Hz from a background thread alongside the torch
upper-body/VLA policy and IK; by default ORT spins up a thread per core, which
starves the real-time control loop and makes rollouts stutter. Cap the pool to
1 intra / 1 inter thread -- lowest-latency for per-step inference -- and quiet
ORT logging.

Co-authored-by: Steven Palma <imstevenpmwork@ieee.org>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(g1): select end effector and camera options through config (#4645)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(g1): select end effector and camera options through config (#4645)

* feat(g1): select the end effector by hardware name

Add an `end_effector` field to UnitreeG1Config taking "dex1", "dex3" or
"dummy". In simulation it selects the MuJoCo model, and with it the finger
actuators and which wrist cameras exist; on the real robot it is for now only a
declaration of what is bolted on, reusing the same name for both paths.

Reaching it needs `make_env` to forward unknown keyword arguments to a hub
env's own `make_env`, since options like this one are defined by the env rather
than by lerobot.

* fix(envs): reject extra make_env arguments for local EnvConfigs

Forwarding unknown keyword arguments to a hub env made them silently harmless
everywhere else: make_env(cfg, n_env=4) used to raise TypeError and instead
built one env, so a misspelt argument became a no-op. Only the hub path has
somewhere to forward to, so the local path now rejects leftovers.

* refactor(envs): carry the G1 end effector in a HubEnvConfig

The flag reached the sim as an extra make_env keyword, which pushed one
env's option into the shared factory signature. Give the sim a
UnitreeG1MujocoEnv config instead: the robot config holds it, make_env
passes it to the hub env untouched, and the sim reads the option off it.
factory.py and utils.py go back to their original signatures, and the
Literal makes the CLI list the three choices and reject anything else.

* feat(envs): carry the G1 sim's camera and viewer options in its config

The sim reads publish_images, camera_port and onscreen off the config the
same way it reads the end effector, so declaring them is all it takes to
reach them from the CLI. onscreen follows publish_images unless it is set,
because the two cannot coexist: the offscreen renderers are bound to the
thread that creates them, and asking for both segfaults the process once
the viewer starts driving MuJoCo.

* docs(g1): document the sim's end effector and camera options

* feat(g1): name the end effector on the robot config

What the arms carry is a property of the robot, not of the simulated world, so
--robot.end_effector is the flag and the hardware paths have somewhere to read
it from once they need to. The sim still takes it off the config it is handed,
which the robot config now keeps in step rather than asking for it twice.

* docs(g1): point at --robot.end_effector

* refactor(g1): fold the end effector into the sim config at the call site

* refactor(g1): set the sim's end effector directly

* refactor(g1): keep the sim's end effector in step from __post_init__

* refactor(envs): make the G1 end effector an enum

Follows ColorMode rather than a Literal alias, so an unknown name reports the
ones that exist. draccus takes either spelling on the CLI, and the member is a
str, which is all the sim asks of it -- it only compares and keys dicts.

* Update docs/source/unitree_g1.mdx

Co-authored-by: Caroline Pascal <caroline8.pascal@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martino Russi <77496684+nepyope@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update src/lerobot/envs/configs.py

Co-authored-by: Caroline Pascal <caroline8.pascal@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martino Russi <77496684+nepyope@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(g1): keep the sim world off the robot's command line

A RobotConfig that reaches an EnvConfig closes a loop in the parser tree: draccus
descends into every choice of every registry it meets, and the gym_manipulator env
carries a RobotConfig of its own. Building the tree then never ends, which broke
every robot CLI, not just the G1's.

Assemble the sim world in __post_init__ instead, from flags that live on the robot,
and cover it with a parse that fails fast if the loop comes back.

* style(g1): tighten the comments on the sim config fields

* Update src/lerobot/envs/configs.py

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(eval): report success counts and 95% Wilson intervals at every a…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(eval): report success counts and 95% Wilson intervals at every aggregation level (#4628)

* feat(eval): report success counts and 95% Wilson intervals at every aggregation level

A success rate over 10 to 50 episodes is a binomial estimate with a wide
interval (9/10 is compatible with roughly 60% to 98%), and lerobot-eval
reported it as a bare number. Every success rate in eval_info.json now
carries n_success, n_episodes and pc_success_ci95 (percent), at task, suite
and overall level, and lerobot-eval logs the overall interval.

lerobot.utils.eval_stats adds wilson_interval, success_summary and a
two-sided fisher_exact, standard library only. Reference values in the tests
were checked against scipy.

Existing keys and values are unchanged. Roadmap EVAL-01 (#3832).

* docs: run the eval_stats docstring examples in CI (first entry in the doctest allowlist)

* fix(eval): drop the unused confidence argument from success_summary

Addresses review finding 1. success_summary took a confidence argument but
always wrote the result under pc_success_ci95, so success_summary(flags,
confidence=0.9) returned a 90% interval under a key that says 95. Nothing
passed it, so the argument is gone and the coverage is fixed at 95%, which
makes the key name always true. wilson_interval keeps the argument for callers
that want a different level.

Also rewords the test comment (finding 5): eval_policy yields Python bools
today, and the test accepts 0/1 ints so a future change to the reduction cannot
silently change what gets counted. The old wording sent readers looking for a
backend that does not exist.

Co-authored-by: Pepijn <138571049+pkooij@users.noreply.github.com>
